newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gemini becomes Macau's fourth cargo airline.
newsitem.headline: Gemini becomes Macau's fourth cargo airline.

text.p: Macau International airport said a fourth cargo airline, Gemini Air Cargo, is now using the airport on a regular basis.

Gemini flew its first McDonnell Douglas DC-10-30 freighter with 65 tonnes capacity into the Portuguese colony on Friday afternoon carrying about 40 tonnes of freight from New York mostly destined for Hong Kong.
The aircraft had flown via Chicago and Anchorage. Gemini said it expects to operate four flights a week between the U.S. and Macau by end-1996.
Unlike Hong Kong which has severe space and slot restrictions, Macau has modern facilities available around the clock.
Macau's other scheduled cargo operators are Scandinavian Airlines System, EVA Air of Taiwan and South Korea's Asiana Airlines which started services earlier this month.
U.S.-based Gemini is a newly established indirect air carrier offering its aircraft to other carriers on wet lease contracts known as ACMI -- aircraft, crew, maintenance and insurance.
Mike English, Gemini's senior vice president, said he was enthusiastic about the potential of the new service and Macau's inter-modal cargo facilities.
"Currently we have set up a contract for freight to be shipped from Hong Kong to Macau by boat prior to being flown to the U.S.," he said.

"What most freight forwarders don't realise is the shipping time from Hong Kong to Macau is only four hours. The flexibility offered by Macau airport's 24 hour operation allows us to be time-constrained only by the customer's needs, and not by airport time and slot problems," he added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
